judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad grant followed by eight carve-outs, several of which are open-textured — 'any unpaid, unrecoverable or outstanding loan ... or any forgiveness of debt', 'restitution, disgorgement, or payment of similar sums', 'matters which are uninsurable under the law' — and in a failed-bank claim the reach of the loan-loss and depreciation carve-outs is precisely the sort of general/specific fight courts resolve.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be squared with the Insuring Agreements' promise to pay Loss the Insureds are legally obligated to pay and with the Fiduciary endorsement's differently worded replacement Loss definition (c153), which drops carve-outs (5) and (6) altogether.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short definition of loss run data; 'potential Claims' is slightly loose but the term is used only administratively.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It feeds only Section XVI(H)'s ten-day production duty and conflicts with nothing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The first named entity set forth of Item 1' contains a preposition slip but the meaning is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The name-change endorsement (c025) inserts Vantus Bank ahead of First Federal Bankshares, silently moving the Named Insured role that governs cancellation, notice and Section XVI(D) authorisation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed list of four constituent documents.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It differs slightly from the Declarations' integration sentence (c018) and Section XVI(B), but all three name essentially the same documents.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defined by reference to Item 2 dates plus 'any earlier termination date'; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item 2 was amended once (c020), and the Discovery Period Activation fixes termination at 05/13/2009, all of which the definition accommodates.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The final sentence — an extension becomes part of the Policy Year 'which would have ended on the original expiration date' — is a fiction that is hard to apply, and the first sentence's 'lesser period' rule pulls the other way.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The one-month extension effected by c020 and the Discovery Period deeming rule in Section III (claims deemed made in the immediately preceding Policy Year) turn this definition into the hinge for which annual limit applies.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Include but are not limited to any solid, liquid, gaseous or thermal organism, irritant or contaminant' is an expressly open-ended list whose outer boundary is undefined — a textbook catch-all problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is used only in the Pollution Exclusion and does not clash with any other provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two alternative registration criteria, each objectively verifiable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used only in the Brokerage/Advisory Services definition; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is scrambled so that limb (1) precedes the words 'Subsidiary means', and the ownership thresholds are inconsistent — 'more than fifty percent' in (1) and (3) but 'fifty percent or more' in (2).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The definition drives the Company definition, the Subsidiary Wrongful Acts exclusion and the Conversion provision's 50% asset tests, which use the concept consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb (5), 'trustee exercising any other trust or fiduciary powers permitted by law', is a broad catch-all sitting after four detailed enumerations, inviting an ejusdem generis argument about the exclusion's reach.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It defines the scope of the Trust Department Services Exclusion and interacts with the IRA/Keogh carve-out in Wrongful Act (2), which expressly sits 'outside of the scope of any Trust Department'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Acting solely in the capacity as such' is the classic capacity limitation that generates argument, and limb (3) makes entity Wrongful Acts contingent on coverage being granted, which is circular.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Limb (2) is cross-referenced by Section VII(A)(4) and Declarations Item 11 for IRA/Keogh claims, but no IRA/Keogh coverage is scheduled, leaving that machinery idling.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line statement that the following exclusions apply to all Insureds under all Insuring Agreements.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Three endorsements delete or replace particular Section V exclusions for their own coverages, so 'all Insuring Agreements' is qualified elsewhere, though expressly so.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The catalogue extends to 'damage to or destruction of any tangible or intangible property', a phrase broad enough to capture ordinary economic loss and thus contestable in scope.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It applies across all Insuring Agreements but does not contradict any grant of coverage in terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Arising out of or in any way involving' is a deliberately broad causal link whose outer limit is a familiar battleground, though the defined service term anchors it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Brokerage endorsement (c131) deletes this exclusion for its own Insuring Agreement, so its residual effect on Insuring Agreements A-C must be read together with that deletion.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Acting independently of, and totally without the solicitation, assistance, participation, or intervention of any Insured' is a demanding and fact-laden standard, with 'assistance' undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates the proviso in Insured vs. Insured limb (3) yet is drafted as a stand-alone bar on all security-holder claims, which is broader than that exclusion's structure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb (3), 'any other violation of any statutory or common law relating to employment', is an open catch-all following two lists of specifics — the paradigm general-versus-specific problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps the ERISA Exclusion and the Fiduciary endorsement's employment-law exclusion, but those are cumulative rather than contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any Claim arising out of or in any way involving any pension, profit sharing or employee benefit program' is broad enough to reach claims with only incidental benefit-plan facts.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Fiduciary endorsement grants precisely the coverage this exclusion removes and deletes the exclusion (c154), so the two only cohere if the deletion is read as coverage-specific.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The second sentence's exception for the 'foreclosure process' and one-to-four family residential property is arguably wide enough to consume the exclusion, since foreclosed property is normally acquired through that process.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits alongside the Loss carve-out for unrecoverable loans (c051(3)) and the Legal Lending Limit exclusion, which address lending losses from different angles.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Provided a final judgment or adjudication establishes' does not say whether the adjudication must be in the underlying action, and 'other than Defense Costs' leaves the repayment consequence unstated — both recurrent points of argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section XV(C)(2) imputes senior officers' knowledge to the Company for this exclusion and the Illegal Profit exclusion, so the two must be read together; the advancement/repayment mechanics sit in Section IX(B)(1).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb (3) excludes claims involving 'conflicts of interest, engaging in self-dealing, or acting in bad faith' with only the words 'in fact' as a qualifier and no adjudication requirement, leaving the trigger genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The neighbouring Fraud exclusion requires a final adjudication while this one does not, an asymmetry that has to be reconciled with Section XV(C)(2)'s imputation rule covering both.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A defined-term exclusion with a narrow parenthetical carve-out; reasonably tight.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The carve-out matches the identical exception in the Brokerage/Advisory Services definition, so the instrument is consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'By, on behalf of, or at the behest of the Company ... or any Insured Person in any capacity', subject to three enumerated exceptions, is the most heavily litigated phrase in D&O policies: whether a successor, receiver or assignee sues 'on behalf of' the Company is genuinely contestable, and the closed list of exceptions invites an expressio unius argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It has to be reconciled with the Financial Impairment definition (c046), which expressly contemplates a receiver taking control of the Company, with Section XVI(I) (Financial Impairment shall not release the Insurer), and with Section VII(B)(1)(b) — all of which assume coverage survives receivership.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Broad but conventional pollution language resting on the open-ended Pollutants definition; the tail 'including Claims alleging damage to the Company or its security holders' is unusual but clear in aim.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision grants pollution-related coverage that this would contradict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The exclusion turns on notice given to 'any carrier other than the Insurer under any similar insurance policy', and 'similar' is left undefined while the Interrelated Wrongful Acts hook is itself elastic.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It runs alongside Section X(B)'s circumstance-notice mechanism and the Prior and Pending Litigation exclusion, which use different temporal anchors.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The same or substantially the same fact, circumstance or situation underlying or alleged in such prior litigation' is a vague, judgment-laden test, and 'litigation ... initiated' is not defined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on the Item 12 dates, which are populated for some Insuring Agreements and 'N/A' for others, so its operation on unscheduled coverages is uncertain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A tightly drawn statutory exclusion tied to Section 16(b).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coheres with the Illegal Profit exclusion and the Securities Liability endorsement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The exclusion is intelligible on its face, though 'in whole or in part at any time when the entity was not a Subsidiary' is a compressed temporal test.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It excepts claims 'as provided in Section XII (C)(3)', but Section XII(C) contains only limbs (1) and (2), and the Discovery Period Activation deletes Section XII altogether — a broken cross-reference on both counts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Broad 'in any way involving' wording anchored to a defined services term whose limb (5) is itself a catch-all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits the Wrongful Act definition's IRA/Keogh carve-out, which expressly operates outside the Trust Department.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short scoping sentence; 'if coverage is set forth on the Declarations' is a plain condition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: These exclusions are stated to apply only under Insuring Agreement (C), yet the endorsements re-import most of them for their own agreements, which is consistent but requires cross-reading.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Brought directly or indirectly by or for the benefit of any insurance carrier' is broad, but the class of claimants is identified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is repeated verbatim in three endorsements, which is duplicative but not contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The proviso 'unless such liability would be imposed regardless of the existence of such contract' is a counterfactual test that is notoriously hard to apply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps the Loss definition's carve-out (5) for contractual obligations, which uses a different formula and its own reimbursement proviso.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Disputes over fees, commissions, or charges' is a compact and reasonably bounded category.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates the Loss definition's carve-out (7) for the return of fees and commissions, so the same subject is addressed twice by different mechanisms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb (1) excludes any Claim 'in any way involving' the Financial Impairment of the Company, which — given that Financial Impairment means receivership — is broad enough to swallow entity coverage for a failed bank.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It pulls directly against Section XVI(I) ('Financial Impairment of the Insured ... shall not release the Insurer from its obligations'), Section VIII(B)(3) and Section VII(B)(1)(b), all of which assume coverage continues through insolvency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three specific service categories, the third ending in 'or provider of like services', a modest catch-all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No coverage grant elsewhere addresses internet services, so nothing conflicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb (6), 'any other investment banking activity', is a general catch-all appended to five specifics, which is exactly the ejusdem generis structure courts are asked to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It carves out securities issued by the Company in limb (1), dovetailing with the Securities Liability endorsement rather than contradicting it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise regulatory test measured 'at the time of its making'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It complements the Loss definition's unrecoverable-loan carve-out without conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A narrow, concrete condition about physical appearance at notarisation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the Policy addresses notarisation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Company's function or activity as receiver, trustee in bankruptcy, or assignee for the benefit of creditors' could be read as limited to the Company acting in those roles, or pressed more broadly where a receiver stands in the Company's shoes.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: In a policy whose Financial Impairment definition and Section XVI(I) both contemplate a receiver being appointed over the Company, the boundary between this exclusion and continued coverage is a genuine whole-instrument question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single, concrete subject matter.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision addresses safe deposit operations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb (2) refers to 'the D&O Limit of Liability set forth in Item 8', a term used nowhere else, and limbs (2)-(3) turn on Item 7 'unless otherwise specified', which in the Declarations is populated with 'N/A' rather than an 'X'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Item 8 limits total far more than the Item 3 Total Policy Limit, and Section VIII(A)'s non-erosion rule also switches on Item 7, so the aggregation scheme has to be reconstructed across several provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The presumptive-indemnification rule ('regardless of whether actual indemnification ... is granted') and the Financial Impairment escape hatch are compressed, and limb (3) says both that retentions are summed and that the total cannot exceed the largest applicable retention.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Limb (3)'s two sentences pull against each other, and the Discovery Period Activation (c004) adds a differently worded acquiring-entity version of limb (2) for the same subject.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The relation-back rule is stated clearly, but its final clause deems a single Claim first made on the earliest date 'regardless of whether such date is before or during the Policy Period', which has an odd effect if that date precedes inception.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That deeming can defeat the Insuring Agreements' requirement that a Claim be 'first made during the Policy Period or the Discovery Period', a tension with Section I and with Section X(B)'s separate relation-back rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It uses 'a sublimit of the D&O Policy', a phrase not defined anywhere, and conditions the whole provision on a separate limit being 'set forth in Item 7'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item 7 of the Declarations contains 'N/A' entries rather than the 'X' the form contemplates, so whether the non-erosion protection applies at all depends on reading the Declarations against Section VII(A).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'In the Insurer's judgment could reasonably exceed' vests a discretionary trigger in the Insurer, which is arguable but the payment order itself is precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coheres with the Non-Erosion provision and Section VIII(B)(3)'s insolvency assurance.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall not incur Defense Costs ... without the Insurer's prior written consent' is a stringent bar sitting beside a 'not unreasonably withheld' qualifier and a right to 'effectively associate' — workable but with soft edges.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The prohibition on incurring Defense Costs without consent sits awkwardly with Section IX(B)(1)'s duty to advance Defense Costs on a current basis and with the no-duty-to-defend structure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Except when advancement ... is prohibited by law or regulation' and the repayment condition 'in the event it is established' leave open who establishes it and how.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is expressly made 'Subject to Section XIV', whose arbitration limb also requires interim advancement, so the two mesh but must be read together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It combines an elastic standard ('as soon as practicable') with a hard 60-day outer limit, and makes both a condition precedent — a familiar site of argument about which controls.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Applied to a 365-day Discovery Period the 60-day cap can bite well before the reporting period ends, and Section III separately bars circumstance notices given during that period.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The specificity requirement ('full particulars as to the names, dates, and persons ... the identity of the potential plaintiffs and the causes of action to be asserted') is exacting and its sufficiency is inherently contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section III expressly disables this mechanism during the Discovery Period, and the relation-back is to a 'Policy Year' whose boundaries are themselves affected by the extension in c020.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pointer to Item 5; the OCR gap does not create real ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Declarations Item 5 and the notice provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All information reasonably requested' and 'such information, assistance and cooperation as the Insurer may reasonably request' are broad but qualified by reasonableness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reinforces Section IX(A)(2) and IX(B)(2) information rights and Section XVI(F)'s full-compliance condition.
